transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-03-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Rios (Polaris CTO), Priya Singh (Polaris Lead SecOps), Liam O'Connor (Polaris Platform Eng)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Polaris wants to understand Redwood's security posture across hosting modes. Main asks: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML/SCIM, RBAC isolation per-tenant, audit logs export to Splunk/Datadog, encryption and customer-managed KMS, data retention options and legal hold.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we really appreciate you taking the time. I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Ravi who is our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:18] Evan: Hey Maya, Evan here, CTO at Polaris. We've got Priya and Liam with me. Priya runs SecOps, Liam's on infra.
[00:25] Priya: Hi all. We've got a pretty strict compliance runway, so looking to nail down hosting choices.
[00:34] Ravi: Great, thanks. High-level agenda is security posture, hosting models, and then run through specific controls like SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and encryption. We'll capture action items and next steps.
[00:46] Liam: Good. I'll flag constraints: we need customer-managed keys for certain datasets and we may be blocked from public hosted endpoints for PII.
[00:55] Maya: Understood. Evan, are you leaning Private from day one or is Dedicated an option?
[01:05] Evan: Preference is Private because of residency and contractual language, but if Dedicated with KMS and VPC peering meets our audit requirements we could consider it to move faster.
[01:18] Priya: Timeline is tight — SOC2 readiness review in Q2. We need artifacts and an architecture show to the auditors.
[01:28] Ravi: We're SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 attested — we'll send the reports. One nuance: our hosted API does not support customer-managed KMS in the public plane today, but Dedicated and Private can integrate with your KMS/HSM via external key wrap.
[01:46] Priya: When you say "external key wrap" can you expand, I want to make sure keys never transit Redwood-managed systems in clear.
[01:55] Ravi: Sure. For Private we support bring-your-own-KMS where the key material stays in your KMS; Redwood will only receive wrapped keys or use an envelope encryption scheme. I'll put the architecture sketch in an action item.
[02:10] Evan: How about audit logs? We need immutable logs forwarded to our Splunk instance and retention set to seven years for a subset of records.
[02:20] Maya: We can forward audit logs over TLS to your SIEM or S3 bucket. For Dedicated and Private we support long-term retention and legal-hold export. Hosted has a default retention window shorter — we'll send the retention matrix.
[02:35] Priya: Is the audit log schema documented? We have requirements for user identity mapping and correlative IDs.
[02:43] Ravi: Yes, there is a schema, I'll attach the sample JSON. Note: sometimes speaker labels in transcripts get swapped, offline docs may say KV cache when they mean KMS — just FYI.
[02:56] Liam: For SSO we use SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning. Need to know about session length, reauth cadence, and role mapping.
[03:06] Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. Role mappings are configurable — we have an RBAC layer you can map to your groups, or we can support custom attributes in SAML assertions.
[03:18] Priya: Do you support just-in-time provisioning or do we need SCIM?
[03:22] Ravi: Both. JIT works for ephemeral seats but SCIM is recommended for enterprise automation.
[03:30] Evan: On RBAC—does Redwood isolate tenant data at the application layer only, or do you offer network/compute separation for Dedicated?
[03:40] Ravi: For Hosted it's application-level multi-tenancy with strict logical separation. Dedicated gives you dedicated GPU pools and network isolation. Private offers complete control—it's your VPC, your subnets. We'll call out the differences in a short doc.
[03:55] Priya: And encryption in transit and at rest? We require AES-256 at rest and TLS1.2+ in transit, plus rotation policies.
[04:05] Ravi: We use AES-256 for at-rest encryption. TLS 1.2+ in transit. Key rotation can be orchestrated by your KMS; for BYOK we can honor your rotation cadence.
[04:16] Evan: A couple of other items — auditability of admin activity, who can see prompts and outputs, and retention for model caching.
[04:28] Maya: Good call. We have RBAC to limit admin actions and an "answers redaction" feature for logs if you want to avoid storing sensitive outputs. Caching behavior and KV cache retention can be configured per deployment but we should map that to your retention policy.
[04:45] Priya: Who gets access to the raw logs on Redwood side? Need to confirm minimal access for Redwood engineers.
[04:52] Ravi: Access is role-based and logged. For Dedicated & Private we can restrict to customer-approved SREs and have audit trails. We'll include the access matrix.
[05:03] Evan: Are you able to support in-region private endpoints in EU and APAC? Our contracts require EU residency for EU customers.
[05:12] Maya: Yes — Private can be deployed in-region. Dedicated region availability varies by capacity but we have EU regions planned. We'll share the region map and expected timelines.
[05:24] Liam: Does Private require on-prem hardware or can it be VPC-hosted in our cloud account?
[05:30] Ravi: Private supports both: a cloud VPC deployment where our control plane handshakes with a customer-side data plane, or a fully on-prem package for air-gapped needs.
[05:42] Priya: Regarding compliance artifacts — do you provide the SOC2 auditor's AICPA mapping or just the report? Auditors ask for mapping to our controls.
[05:52] Maya: We'll provide the SOC2 Type II report and a controls mapping deck that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks; sometimes we create a custom mapping for the customer's auditor as a paid engagement — we can discuss if needed.
[06:08] Evan: Ok. On the legal side, what about data deletion guarantees and proofs — e.g., if a user requests deletion, how do you demonstrate data erasure?
[06:18] Ravi: We maintain deletion logs and can provide evidence of deletion operations. For Private you control the underlying storage so you can run validations; for Hosted we maintain deletion records and can provide exportable audit trails.
[06:31] Priya: Does Redwood ever use customer data to fine-tune models or for evals? This is a hard no for us unless explicitly contracted.
[06:39] Maya: Redwood does not use customer data for model training. We'll include a data use clause in the doc.
[06:46] Evan: About legal hold — can we freeze retention windows for a given tenant?
[06:51] Ravi: Yes, we support legal-hold flags that prevent deletion for specific datasets. We'll show the retention matrix which includes legal-hold behavior.
[07:03] Liam: Any rate-limiting/tokenization of logs we should be aware of? Also curious about per-token billing hooks if we do Dedicated.
[07:12] Maya: We'll send a token-level billing breakdown and latency/throughput SLOs per Dedicated tier. Tokenization of logs is optional; we can redact tokens before storing.
[07:22] Priya: Do you provide SIEM connectors out of the box?
[07:26] Ravi: We have native connectors for Splunk and Datadog and a generic S3/SQS export pattern for other SIEMs.
[07:35] Evan: On the SAML side we need to validate signature algorithms and cert rotation — any limitations?
[07:42] Ravi: We support standard RSA-SHA256 signatures and cert rotation. We also support enforcing signed assertions.
[07:51] Maya: Let's talk about the pivot decision — if we do Dedicated with KMS and VPC peering can you sign the SOC2/ISO requirement off, or does the auditor need Private?
[08:00] Priya: Our auditor tends to prefer customer-controlled cryptography and network boundaries. If Dedicated provides customer-managed KMS and peering with strict egress rules, it might pass, but we'll need to show the mapping to controls.
[08:13] Ravi: Understood. We'll prepare both a Dedicated and Private control mapping and indicate gaps.
[08:22] Evan: Great. Can you also include expected lead times — Dedicated provisioning and Private deployment timelines?
[08:29] Maya: Typical Dedicated lead time is 4–6 weeks after contract; Private can range 6–12 weeks depending on VPC complexity and KMS integration. We'll include that in the follow-up.
[08:41] Liam: For the BYOK with HSM, do you support HSMs from AWS CloudHSM and Azure Key Vault HSM?
[08:49] Ravi: Yes, we support AWS KMS and CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault, and customer HSMs that expose standard PKCS#11 interfaces. There are some caveats around latency and key wrapping — we'll detail them.
[09:01] Priya: About monitoring — we want access to per-model inference telemetry and operator audit trails integrated into our dashboards.
[09:09] Maya: Those telemetry hooks are available in Dedicated and Private. We can stream metrics and traces to your endpoints and provide dashboards in Redwood Console.
[09:20] Evan: Any known limitations with quantized models and logging? We have workloads that use 4-bit quantization to reduce cost, does that change caching or logging?
[09:30] Ravi: Not generally. Quantization affects inference execution but not audit logs. We will call out any model variant differences.
[09:38] Priya: Ok, thanks. I think we have a good set of artifacts to review.
[09:43] Maya: Awesome. Quick recap and actions?
[09:46] Ravi: I'll produce the Private deployment sketch with BYOK details and sample log schema.
[09:50] Maya: I'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts and Dedicated pricing tiers.
[09:53] Priya: We'll send our retention policy and any auditor questions by next Tuesday.
[09:58] Evan: Let's tentatively schedule a technical deep dive for 2027-03-15.
[10:03] Maya: Sounds good, we'll follow up with a calendar invite and the docs.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings; e.g., "KV cache" spoken as "K V cache" in places, proper nouns like "Polaris" sometimes transcribed as "Polar ice".

End of transcript.
